content: The synonymous mutation associated with intrinsic pyrazinamide (PZA) resistance in Mycobacterium canettii was reclassified as a Group 4 mutation. However, a footnote was added to indicate that M. canettii may be present, to reduce the risk of missing intrinsic PZA resistance in assays that analyze the pncA gene but not other loci for differentiating members of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC). The sensitivity estimates for pncA mutations were based on relaxed grading criteria rather than the standard criteria used for other drugs. In the first edition, an additional grading criterion was proposed but not endorsed, which would have increased sensitivity by assuming that any coding pncA mutation, except silent mutations and Group 4 or 5 mutations, was a valid marker of resistance if it occurred in genotypically rifampin-resistant isolates. The WHO-endorsed GenoType MTBDRsl assay for PZA resistance relies on inferring resistance, as it cannot differentiate most pncA mutations. In settings where non-silent but neutral pncA mutations are more frequent, the specificity and positive predictive value (PPV) of the assay may decrease significantly. Silent mutations, except for pncA 138A>G, are not listed in the catalog but can be found in the master file. It is important to consider that certain variants might indicate the isolate is M. canettii, which is intrinsically PZA-resistant. For fluoroquinolone (FQ) resistance, the most significant change in the second edition was the upgrading of gyrA Asp89Asn and three gyrB mutations (Ser447Phe, Asn499Thr, and Asp461His) to low-level resistance mutations. All gyrA and gyrB mutations were classified as conferring low-level resistance to moxifloxacin (MFX), except for high-level resistance mutations such as gyrA Gly88Cys, Asp94Asn, Asp94Gly, Asp94His, and Asp94Tyr. Genetically linked low-level resistance mutations likely have additive effects and should be considered high-level resistant. For bedaquiline (BDQ) and clofazimine (CFZ), no mutations met Group 1 or 2 grading criteria for resistance prediction in the first edition. Six atpE mutations (Asp28Ala, Asp28Gly, Asp28Val, Glu61Asp, Ile66Met, and Ala63Pro) were classified as Group 2 resistance mutations. Notably, two of these mutations (Ala63Pro and Ile66Met) occurred as solo mutations at sufficient frequency to meet thresholds for association with phenotypic resistance, indicating that atpE mutations can arise independently of Rv0678 mutations. The remaining four atpE mutations met criteria based on in vitro selection experiments, supporting the additional grading rule that any loss-of-function (LoF) mutation in Rv0678 and pepQ was assumed to confer BDQ resistance. The laboratory contributing most BDQ phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) results to the WHO dataset only submitted categorical results for isolates resistant at two independent laboratories. This may have inflated the PPV of mutations in these isolates, as no BDQ-susceptible isolates were submitted from this collection. For example, the grading of the Rv0678 Met146Thr mutation, frequent in Eswatini but rare elsewhere, was potentially affected by this isolate collection. This mutation was initially graded as Group 1 based on a PPV of 100% in the WHO dataset, calculated from 12 resistant isolates. However, MIC results from another laboratory suggested a lower PPV of 67%, which was not considered in the WHO dataset. Given these results, the working group downgraded all Group 1 BDQ mutations meeting criteria based solely on results from the primary laboratory to Group 2. A footnote was added to identify 18 mutations with potentially inflated PPVs. The remaining 15 mutations would have been classified as Group 2 even without data from the primary laboratory, as they were covered by the Rv0678 or pepQ LoF grading rule, supported by in vitro selection data, or classified based on the ALL dataset. Published evidence suggests that Rv0678 mutations confer resistance only if the corresponding efflux pump is functional. Loss-of-function mutations in mmpL5, which may be frequent in some settings, can confer a hyper-susceptible phenotype to BDQ and CFZ. Consequently, assays targeting only Rv0678 should include a disclaimer acknowledging the potential impact of epistasis on the predictive power of Rv0678 mutations. The dataset did not include any mmpS5 LoF mutants with BDQ pDST results, so their role in epistasis could not be investigated. For delamanid (DLM) and pretomanid (PMD), the ddn Leu49Pro mutation was the only mutation classified as Group 2 for DLM resistance in both the first and second editions. Pooled ddn LoF mutations met Group 2 criteria in the ALL dataset. LoF mutations in five other resistance genes (fbiA, fbiB, fbiC, fgd1, and Rv2983) were also recognized as Group 2 mutations for DLM based on laboratory selection, complementation, and knockdown experiments.
